title: Earth's Features and Maps
seo_title: Grade 4 Earth's Features Worksheets: Mountains, Volcanoes, Earthquakes and Map Patterns
standard_text: Analyze and interpret data from maps to describe patterns of Earth's features.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 science worksheets on Earth's features and maps (NGSS 4-ESS2-2): map keys and elevation maps, patterns of mountains, volcanoes and earthquakes, the Ring of Fire, ocean ridges and trenches. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Earth's features form patterns on maps.
key_sub: Many volcanoes and earthquakes lie in long bands, like the Ring of Fire around the Pacific. Mountains often form chains.
body_html:
How to think about it

Maps show where Earth's features are. Read the map key to learn what each symbol and color means, and use the compass rose for directions.

Earth's features are not spread out evenly. They form patterns:

  • Many volcanoes and earthquakes are in long bands, like the Ring of Fire around the Pacific Ocean.
  • Mountain chains often run along the edges of continents, like the Andes and the Rockies.
  • The ocean floor has ridges (underwater mountain chains) and trenches (very deep valleys).
Example

A map shows earthquake dots in a band around the Pacific Ocean. What is the pattern?

The dots are not everywhere.

They follow the edge of the Pacific.

Answer: Most earthquakes are around the edges of the Pacific.

Example

On an elevation map, dark brown means over 1,000 m. A line of dark brown runs north to south. What is it?

Dark brown = high land.

Answer: a mountain range

Common mistakes

  • Thinking volcanoes and earthquakes are spread evenly over Earth.
  • Thinking the ocean floor is flat.
  • Forgetting to read the map key before answering.

faq.q: What patterns do maps show about volcanoes and earthquakes?
faq.a: They are mostly found in long bands, such as the Ring of Fire around the Pacific Ocean, not spread evenly over Earth.

faq.q: What features are on the ocean floor?
faq.a: Mid-ocean ridges (long underwater mountain chains), deep trenches, and wide flat plains.

faq.q: How do you read an elevation map?
faq.a: Use the map key. Each color stands for a range of heights, so you can find mountains and low land.

items.q: What is a trench?
c: a long, very deep valley in the ocean floor
items.e: Trenches are the deepest parts of the ocean.

items.e: Patterns on maps help us make predictions.
